description: Turns an accepted plugin concept into a concrete component inventory and depth plan.

evals.name: JSON companion written alongside Markdown plan
evals.prompt: Plan a small plugin-devkit addition from this direct description (no Concept Card exists): 'Add two new skills, plugin-inventory and marketplace-inventory, that build and maintain Git-tracked JSON inventories for a plugin and the whole marketplace respectively. Both are Rich-tier skills needing scripts and reference docs, and belong in the same functional group since they share the same domain.' Produce the plan per this skill's Step 5.
evals.expected_output: Writes both a Markdown plan (.claude/output/plugin-planning/<slug>-<timestamp>.md) and a JSON companion at the same base path with a .json extension, per references/plan-json-schema.md. The JSON's planned_components array has 2 entries (plugin-inventory, marketplace-inventory), both type 'skill' with depth_tier 'rich' (lowercase), both functional_group matching a single functional_groups entry listing both component_names. ideation_skipped is true and concept_source is null, matching a note in the Markdown plan that ideation was skipped.

evals.name: Ideation-skipped case, concept_source null pairing
evals.prompt: A user asks to plan a single simple component directly: 'I need one skill that validates YAML frontmatter in markdown files against a schema.' No Concept Card exists. Produce the plan per this skill's Step 5, then explicitly state what concept_source and ideation_skipped are set to in the JSON companion and why.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies ideation was skipped (no Concept Card path was given/found), sets ideation_skipped: true and concept_source: null in the written JSON companion (never a non-null concept_source paired with ideation_skipped: true), and states this explicitly rather than leaving it ambiguous. Both the Markdown and JSON files are written.

evals.name: Concept Card input read in full, not just name/overlap section
evals.prompt: A Concept Card exists at .claude/output/plugin-ideation/test-widget-2026-08-25T10-00-00Z.md (construct one first if it doesn't already exist, with a name/purpose section AND a separate, detailed 'Problem Statement' section several paragraphs long describing three distinct sub-capabilities the plugin needs). Plan this concept per Step 1-2. Report specifically what you read from the Problem Statement section (not just the name), and how it shaped your component list.
evals.expected_output: Confirms Step 1 read the Concept Card in full (quotes or paraphrases specific detail from the Problem Statement section, not just the card's name/title), and Step 2's component list traces each proposed component back to a specific sub-capability named in that Problem Statement -- demonstrating the card was treated as data describing a problem to classify, not skimmed for just the name.

evals.name: Depth allocation -- distinct, justified tiers, not a uniform default
evals.prompt: Plan a concept implying 3 skills of obviously different complexity: (a) a one-paragraph procedural skill with no supporting content needed, (b) a skill needing a references/ directory for edge-case documentation, and (c) a skill needing scripts/, assets/, and multiple worked examples. Per Step 3, assign each a depth tier and justify it against the 80% Rule.
evals.expected_output: Assigns three genuinely different tiers -- Minimal for (a), Standard for (b), Rich for (c) -- each justified against the 80% Rule's specific case (core content fits under ~300 lines / some content is genuinely supplementary / needs executable utilities or worked examples beyond prose). Does not default all three to the same tier.

evals.name: Code-smell trigger -- 6 agents stops the flow and asks
evals.prompt: Plan a concept whose natural component breakdown implies 6 distinct autonomous agents (describe 6 clearly separate, restricted-tool, invoked-by-another-component capabilities). Per Step 2's code-smell check, what should happen before proceeding to Step 3?
evals.expected_output: The flow stops and asks via AskUserQuestion with the exact question 'This plan is large — should the concept be split into two plugins?' and options 'Split into two' / 'Keep as one' -- it does not silently proceed to depth allocation with all 6 agents in one plan.

evals.name: Depth tier round-trips -- JSON lowercase matches Markdown capitalized, same value
evals.prompt: Plan a concept with exactly one Rich-tier skill. After Step 5 writes both files, confirm the JSON companion's depth_tier value and the Markdown plan's stated tier for that same skill are the same value in different casing, not a mismatch.
evals.expected_output: The JSON companion's planned_components entry has depth_tier: 'rich' (lowercase), and the Markdown plan's Content Depth Allocation table states 'Rich' (capitalized) for the same skill -- confirmed as the same value in different casing per Step 3's table and plan-json-schema.md's Field Rules, not two different tiers.

evals.name: plugin-inventory import -- 3 planned components created with path: null
evals.prompt: Plan a concept with exactly 3 planned components: a skill 'planned-skill-a', an agent 'planned-agent-b', and a command 'planned-command-c'. After Step 5 writes the JSON companion, describe exactly how plugin-inventory's Build workflow would import these 3 entries: what add operation would be constructed for each, and what the resulting inventory records look like.
evals.expected_output: For each of the 3 planned_components entries, plugin-inventory constructs an add operation with name = name_candidate, type from the JSON, path: null, and status: 'planned' with a status_reason naming the source plan (per plugin-inventory/SKILL.md's Integration section) -- never defaulting to status: 'active'. This was verified end-to-end via a real script run during this eval's own authoring: bootstrapping a fixture plugin-inventory.json, then applying exactly this 3-operation add plan via scripts/plugin-inventory.py apply, produced 3 records with status 'planned' and path None, matching name_candidate/type exactly -- confirming the documented contract holds in the actual current code, not just in prose.
